key_insight: DynamicVLA combines a compact 0.4B vision-language-action backbone with explicit temporal reasoning and closed-loop adaptation so a single model can perceive, anticipate, and continuously control in dynamic object manipulation tasks. The result is real-time, robust handling of moving objects without large model sizes.
problem_solved: Vision-Language-Action models that excel at static manipulation fail in dynamic scenarios that demand fast perception, temporal anticipation, and continuous corrective control; DynamicVLA addresses this gap enabling reliable manipulation of moving objects.
method: Compact VLA backbone (≈0.4B parameters) with a convolutional vision encoder for spatial efficiency and low-latency visual feature extraction.
Temporal reasoning module that models short-term dynamics and anticipates object motion across video frames to inform action planning.
Closed-loop adaptation/control loop that continuously fuses perception and action feedback for online correction and robust execution in dynamic environments.
impact: Provides a lightweight, practical architecture for deploying VLA capabilities in real-time robotic manipulation and embodied systems, lowering compute and latency barriers for dynamic interactions.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: camera frames → conv vision encoder → temporal reasoning → action policy → actuator, with a feedback arrow closing the loop.
Sequence visualization: side-by-side frames showing model anticipation/prediction of future object positions and resulting corrective actions.
Closed-loop schematic: timing/latency icons showing low-latency perception and continuous control updates.
Performance sketch: simple bar or radar chart comparing robustness/latency/param size vs. baseline static VLA models.
paper_title: DynamicVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation
paper_authors: Haozhe Xie, Beichen Wen, Jiarui Zheng, Zhaoxi Chen, Fangzhou Hong
